content: Stanley Medical College (SMC) is a government-run medical institution located in Chennai, Tamil Nadu, India. The college is associated with hospitals and has a rich history in medical education. Although the original hospital dates back over 200 years, the medical college was officially established on July 2, 1938. It is ranked 9th among the top medical colleges in India, according to NDTV rankings. History Stanley Medical College and its associated hospitals are among the oldest centers for medical education in India. The foundation of this institution was laid as early as 1740 when the East India Company established a medical department. The current Stanley Hospital is situated on the site of the old Monegar Choultry, which was established in 1782. In 1809, the Assistant John Native Infirmary was created, incorporating the Monegar Choultry and a leper asylum. In 1830, Raja Sir Ramasamy Mudaliar, a noted philanthropist, endowed a hospital and dispensary within the Native Infirmary. Medical courses such as B.M.M. and S.M. were introduced in the infirmary. By 1903, a hospital assistant course was initiated with the support of the East India Company. The first graduating class received their Licensed Medical Practitioner (LMP) diplomas in 1911. The Diploma in Medicine and Surgery (M. & S.) course was inaugurated by Sir George Frederick Stanley, after whom the institution was named by the Governor of Madras Presidency on July 2, 1928. In 1941, three medical and surgical units were established, which expanded to seven units by 1964. Initially, 100 students were admitted annually in 1932, and this number increased to 150 students per year from 1963. In 1964, Dr. Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan, the President of India, laid the foundation stone for the College Auditorium to commemorate the institution's Silver Jubilee. Description Stanley Medical College is affiliated with the Government Stanley Hospital, which has 1,580 beds for inpatient care. The hospital sees an outpatient attendance of approximately 5,000 patients daily. A unique feature of the hospital is its eight-story surgical complex, which is equipped to perform up to 40 surgeries simultaneously. Additionally, there is a dedicated pediatrics block that houses all pediatric specialties under one roof. The hospital is renowned for its departments of Surgical Gastroenterology, Urology, and the Institute of Hand Rehabilitation and Plastic Surgery. The Institute for Research and Rehabilitation of Hand and the Department of Plastic Surgery (IRRH & DPS) is considered one of the best centers in Southeast Asia. The Department of Surgical Gastroenterology was the first in India to successfully perform a liver transplant under the leadership of Dr. P. Shanmugam. It was also the first hospital department in India to receive ISO 9001 certification. The Department of Urology performs up to 50 kidney transplants annually. Admissions Admissions to the Bachelor of Medicine and Surgery (MBBS) program and postgraduate courses (MD, MS, diplomas, and higher specialties) are conducted through state (85% seats) and national (15% seats) entrance examinations. Reserved seats and reduced tuition fees are available for underserved communities. Admissions are open only to Indian citizens and are highly competitive. For the MBBS program, which has approximately 150 seats per year, selection is based on a weighted aggregate of entrance exam scores and high school final exam scores. Only about 1 in 40 applicants statewide are accepted into the MBBS program, and only the top-ranked students are admitted to Stanley Medical College, making the effective admission rate less than 1 in 200. Several postgraduate seats are reserved for physicians in government service. Postgraduate degrees (MD, MS) involve a three-year residency, while postgraduate diploma programs require a two-year clinical residency. Higher specialty fellowship training programs, such as M.Ch. in Plastic Surgery, are also offered. Attached Hospitals Stanley Medical College is associated with the following hospitals: Government Stanley Hospital, Chennai 600001 Government Raja Sir Ramasamy Mudaliar (RSRM) Lying-in Hospital, Chennai 600013 Government Hospital for Thoracic Medicine, Tambaram, Chennai 600047 Government Peripheral Hospital, Tondiarpet, Chennai 600081 Notable Faculty and Alumni The institution has produced several distinguished alumni and faculty, including: Prof. R. Venkataswami, founder of IRRH & DPS (Hand Rehabilitation/Plastic Surgery) Dr. S. Ramachandran, a prominent brain researcher Dr. T. Thomas, a cardiothoracic surgeon Dr. Mohammed Rela, a renowned liver transplant surgeon at King’s College Hospital Dr. Prathap C. Reddy, founder of Apollo Hospitals Dr. David Jayakar, Director of Cardiothoracic Surgery, Chicago, USA Dr. Dilawar Mistry, Co-Medical Director of Sports Medicine, University of Virginia, and Team Physician for USA Swimming Student Life and Activities Stanley Medical College is known for the camaraderie among its students and the quality of its alumni. The annual alumni reunion, Old Stanleans Day, is held on the last Sunday of January each year. Each MBBS class assigns itself a unique name based on the year of entry, such as Stanley '86 or Aesclepius 1999. The college has an award-winning music group that participates in inter-college cultural festivals. Its annual cultural festival, Euphoria, is popular in Chennai and attracts participants from other states. The college also has hockey, football, and cricket teams. Students publish a monthly magazine, the Stanley Times, showcasing their creative expressions. The Stanley Literary Society promotes literature and arts, while the Rotaract Club provides free medical services to underserved communities. The college also hosts a National Cadet Corps (NCC) company affiliated with the medical division of Tamil Nadu NCC. Student Facilities Separate boarding and lodging facilities are available for male and female students. The men’s hostel has distinct kitchen and dining facilities for undergraduates, house surgeons, and postgraduates. The campus includes excellent sports facilities, such as a turf cricket pitch, a basketball ground, and two tennis courts. The campus is well-maintained with trees and gardens, although many trees were cut down in February 2007 for expansion, altering the campus's once-pleasant and shaded environment.
